A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results from the study suggest that the dose-volume relationships are important for the development of fibrotic changes in the lungs after stereotactic radiation.
the dose-response and dose-volume relationships for radiation-induced fibrosis are complex and depend on the specific tissue, location and time of follow-up.

we can identify a subgroup of patients with a high risk of radiation-induced lung injury.
the dose-response relationship for fibrosis is not linear and that the spatial distribution of fibrosis is not uniform.
